gloss: to devote oneself to; to throw oneself into

definitions.gloss: to devote oneself to; to throw oneself into; to enter (a field or cause)
definitions.explanation: To commit oneself wholeheartedly to a cause, profession, or activity. Implies entering a new world or field with dedication.

definitions.gloss: to throw oneself (physically); to jump into
definitions.explanation: To physically leap or jump into something, such as water or a dangerous situation.

examples.japanese: {政治|せいじ}の{世界|せかい}に{身|み}を{投|とう}じた。
examples.english: He threw himself into the world of politics.

examples.japanese: {若|わか}くして{革命運動|かくめいうんどう}に{身|み}を{投|とう}じた。
examples.english: He devoted himself to the revolutionary movement at a young age.

examples.japanese: {会社|かいしゃ}を{辞|や}めて、{教育|きょういく}の{分野|ぶんや}に{身|み}を{投|とう}じることを{決|き}めた。
examples.english: I quit my job and decided to devote myself to the field of education.

examples.japanese: {川|かわ}に{身|み}を{投|とう}じた。
examples.english: He threw himself into the river.

examples.japanese: {燃|も}える{建物|たてもの}の{中|なか}に{身|み}を{投|とう}じて{子|こ}どもを{助|たす}けた。
examples.english: He threw himself into the burning building and rescued the child.

examples.japanese: {激|はげ}しい{戦|たたか}いの{中|なか}に{身|み}を{投|とう}じることを{恐|おそ}れなかった。
examples.english: He was not afraid to throw himself into the fierce battle.

notes:
Idiomatic expression composed of {身|み} (body, self) + を + {投|とう}じる (to throw, to cast). Literally "to throw one's body/self into." The figurative sense (devoting oneself) is more common than the literal sense.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {政治|せいじ}に{身|み}を{投|とう}じる: to enter politics
- {戦|たたか}いに{身|み}を{投|とう}じる: to throw oneself into battle
- {事業|じぎょう}に{身|み}を{投|とう}じる: to devote oneself to a business venture
- {芸術|げいじゅつ}に{身|み}を{投|とう}じる: to devote oneself to art

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {身|み}を{捧|ささ}げる: to dedicate oneself — emphasizes sacrifice and service
- {打|う}ち{込|こ}む: to throw oneself into — more casual, used for hobbies and interests
- {専念|せんねん}する: to concentrate on — more neutral, less dramatic
